cleanIntro:
The Model 92 is Weatherby's 12-gauge pump. A cross-bolt safety sits at the rear of the trigger guard, and a gold disconnector lever on the right of the receiver unlocks the forearm when the gun is cocked.

Weatherby's strip takes the barrel off forward and upward, then the forearm off the magazine tube with the bolt and carrier riding on its action bars. The trigger assembly and the bolt's locking block come out only in Deep Clean.

This guide follows Weatherby's own MODEL 92 owner's instructions.

steps.title: Safety on: button pushed to the right
steps.action: Point the gun somewhere safe and keep your finger off the trigger. Push the safety button at the rear of the trigger guard through to the right. That is SAFE. Pushed to the left, a red band shows and the gun is ready to fire.
steps.quote: When pressed through the trigger guard to the right
steps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — SAFETY, p.2

steps.title: Cocked gun: disconnector lever forward to free the forearm
steps.action: If the gun is cocked, the forearm is locked and will not move. Push the gold disconnector lever on the right side of the receiver forward and the forearm comes free to move rearward.
steps.quote: If gun is cocked, move disconnector lever forward to permit forearm to move rearward.
steps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO DISASSEMBLE BOLT ASSEMBLY FOR CLEANING, p.5

steps.title: Pump it empty, round by round
steps.action: Push the disconnector lever forward and pull the forearm all the way back. The shell in the chamber ejects and the next one is released from the magazine tube. Roll the gun sideways so the released shell drops out of the ejection port, close the action by moving the forearm forward, and repeat until nothing more comes out.
steps.prose: Then look into the chamber and the magazine tube yourself. Weatherby's own caution here is to check both to be certain the gun is empty.
steps.quote: Push disconnector lever forward and pull forearm
steps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO UNLOAD, p.4

steps.title: Empty and on SAFE before anything comes off
steps.action: Make sure the gun is unloaded and the safety button is in the SAFE position before you start taking it apart.
steps.quote: sure gun is unloaded and safety button is in
steps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO DISASSEMBLE BARREL FROM GUN, p.4

steps.title: Forearm back until the bolt face is halfway open
steps.action: Move the forearm rearward until the bolt face sits about halfway back in the ejection port. This is the position the barrel comes off and goes back on in.
steps.quote: Move forearm rearward until bolt face is halfway open
steps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO DISASSEMBLE BARREL FROM GUN, p.4

steps.title: Magazine cap off, barrel forward and up
steps.action: Unscrew the magazine cap. Pull the barrel gently forward and upward until the barrel extension clears the front of the receiver, and lift it away.
steps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO DISASSEMBLE BARREL FROM GUN, p.4

steps.title: Forearm forward to its stop, lifter pressed up
steps.action: Hold the gun level and pull the forearm forward until it stops. Keep it there and press the lifter up with your right index finger or thumb.
steps.quote: press lifter up with the right index finger or thumb
steps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO DISASSEMBLE BOLT ASSEMBLY FOR CLEANING, p.5

steps.title: ⛔ Gun right side up, then the shell latch on the LEFT
steps.action: Press the shell latch on the left side of the receiver, the side opposite the ejection port. The forearm then slides completely off the magazine tube and brings the bolt assembly out of the receiver with it.
steps.prose: ⛔ You may turn the gun over to find the latch, but turn it right side up again before you press it. Pressed upside down, the bolt assembly drops off the action bars.
steps.quote: before depressing latch and proceeding with disassembly
steps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO DISASSEMBLE BOLT ASSEMBLY FOR CLEANING, p.5

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: With the forearm assembly off the gun, lift the bolt assembly and the bolt carrier off the slide action bars. That is Weatherby's strip for cleaning: barrel, magazine cap, forearm with its action bars, bolt and carrier, and the receiver.
steps.prose: The locking block stays in the bolt for normal cleaning. Taking it out, and taking the trigger assembly out of the receiver, are in Deep Clean.
steps.quote: It is not normally necessary to remove the locking block from the bolt for cleaning
steps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO DISASSEMBLE BOLT ASSEMBLY FOR CLEANING, p.5

steps.title: Every 500 rounds: all accessible parts and the inside of the receiver
steps.action: Weatherby's interval is a strip and clean every 500 rounds: all accessible parts and the inside of the receiver, with any commercial powder solvent or gun cleaner. Then wipe the parts dry.
steps.prose: Dirt and burned and unburned powder left in the gun cause malfunctions in the trigger group and wear parts for nothing.
steps.quote: commercial powder solvents or gun cleaners work very well.
steps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — CLEANING, p.8

steps.title: Choke tube tightened with the wrench, nothing else
steps.action: When a Multi-choke tube goes back in, tighten it with the wrench supplied with the gun before the gun is fired. Another tool can mar or damage the tube.
steps.prose: ⛔ The gun is unloaded and the bolt open before a choke tube goes in or comes out, and a Multi-choke barrel is never fired without a tube in place.
steps.quote: use the wrench provided with the gun to tighten the tube before firing the gun.
steps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — MULTI-CHOKE BARRELS, p.8

steps.title: A light coat on accessible parts, none into the trigger group
steps.action: Put a light coat of oil on the accessible parts and no more than a very thin coat on exposed parts. Do not squirt oil into the trigger group or other crevices.
steps.prose: Oil beyond a thin film holds dirt and debris on the parts.
steps.quote: Do not squirt oil into the trigger group
steps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — CLEANING, p.8

steps.title: Synthetic lubricant, and in cold weather nothing thick
steps.action: Weatherby prefers a modern synthetic lubricant to the older petroleum oils. Below freezing, petroleum products thicken and harden: take off all regular oil and use a synthetic rated for low temperatures, or a dry graphite lubricant, in very thin coats.
steps.quote: modern synthetic lubricant is superior to the older petroleum products
steps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — CLEANING and COLD-WEATHER USE, p.8

deepSteps.title: Trigger assembly: safety on, gun cocked, action closed
deepSteps.action: With the barrel off, make sure the gun is not loaded and put the safety button on SAFE. Cock the gun by pumping the action, and leave the action closed.
deepSteps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO REMOVE TRIGGER, p.7

deepSteps.title: Two pins out from the left, with a punch
deepSteps.action: From the left side of the receiver, tap out the front trigger plate pin with a punch. Then tap out the disconnector lever pin.
deepSteps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO REMOVE TRIGGER, p.7

deepSteps.title: Trigger guard up, rear of the assembly lifted out
deepSteps.action: Turn the gun so the trigger guard faces up. Lift the rear of the trigger assembly out of the receiver until it is completely out.
deepSteps.quote: out of receiver until completely removed
deepSteps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO REMOVE TRIGGER, p.7

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Clean it as one unit, still cocked
deepSteps.action: Leave the trigger assembly cocked and clean it as a unit with solvent. Afterwards wipe it dry and re-oil it lightly. If the trigger gets pulled while you clean, press the hammer back to the cocked position.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Weatherby stops here: the trigger assembly is not taken apart.
deepSteps.quote: Do not attempt to disassemble the unit.
deepSteps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO REMOVE TRIGGER, p.7

deepSteps.title: Front of the assembly in first, then the disconnector lever pin by hand
deepSteps.action: Put the front of the trigger assembly into the action first, then lower the rear gently into the receiver. Check it is aligned, then push the disconnector lever pin in by hand. If it will not go fully home, rotate the pin with the disconnector lever and keep pushing until it seats.
deepSteps.quote: Pin can be pushed into position by hand.
deepSteps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO REMOVE TRIGGER, p.7

deepSteps.title: Front trigger plate pin back to its stop
deepSteps.action: Push the front trigger plate pin back in to its stop, lined up with the hole in the trigger assembly, and tap it home with a plastic hammer until it is fully seated.
deepSteps.quote: Reinsert front trigger plate pin to stop.
deepSteps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO REMOVE TRIGGER, p.7

deepSteps.title: Locking block, only if it has to come out: firing-pin retaining pin first
deepSteps.action: Weatherby does not recommend taking the locking block out of the bolt for cleaning. If you must, punch the firing-pin retaining pin out of the bolt from top to bottom.
deepSteps.quote: Punch out firing-pin retaining pin from top to bottom
deepSteps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO DISASSEMBLE BOLT ASSEMBLY FOR CLEANING, p.5

deepSteps.title: Firing pin and spring out
deepSteps.action: Take out the firing pin and its spring.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin and spring
deepSteps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO DISASSEMBLE BOLT ASSEMBLY FOR CLEANING, p.5

deepSteps.title: Locking block out of the bottom of the bolt
deepSteps.action: Remove the locking block from the bottom of the bolt.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the locking block from the bottom of the bolt
deepSteps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO DISASSEMBLE BOLT ASSEMBLY FOR CLEANING, p.5

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Back in reverse order, cross pin in place
deepSteps.action: Reassemble the bolt in reverse order, and make sure the cross pin that passes through the locking block is in place.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ The locking block must be back in the bolt before the gun is reassembled and fired. Fired without it, the gun is damaged and you can be hurt.
deepSteps.cite: Weatherby MODEL 92 owner's instructions — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — TO DISASSEMBLE BOLT ASSEMBLY FOR CLEANING, p.5

cleaning.name: RECEIVER AND BOLT
tasks: Inside of the receiver cleaned with powder solvent or gun cleaner
Bolt, carrier and action bars cleaned and wiped dry
Locking block left in the bolt unless it has to come out

cleaning.name: BARREL AND CHOKE TUBES
tasks: Bore cleaned and looked through: clear of any obstruction
Choke tube back in and tightened with the supplied wrench
⛔ Never fire a Multi-choke barrel without a tube in place

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE TUBE
tasks: Magazine tube wiped nearly dry with a clean cloth

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: A light coat of oil on accessible parts
Do not squirt oil into the trigger group or other crevices
In freezing weather, all regular oil off; low-temperature synthetic or dry graphite, very thin

reassembly: Bolt body over the carrier, locking block already in it: the carrier's large flat surface toward the front of the bolt, its step toward the back.
Carrier and bolt into the grooves of the slide action bars, front of the bolt facing the front of the forearm.
Bolt lined up with the receiver, forearm pushed onto the magazine tube, then eased rearward until the bolt stops about halfway into the action.
Hand on the forearm, press the lifter fully down and press the shell latch on the left; ease the forearm back until it stops again.
Press the shell latch on the ejection-port side and move the forearm rearward to its stop.
Disconnector lever forward, forearm rearward to open the action fully, then back to the halfway position for the barrel.
Barrel extension into the front of the receiver with the magazine ring guide lined up on the magazine tube; slide the barrel gently back until it butts solidly against the receiver.
Magazine cap screwed on finger tight.
fncheck: Prove it empty at the chamber and the magazine tube. Work the action through several times for free travel. Safety on SAFE (pushed to the right), trigger: nothing. With the gun cocked the forearm should stay locked until the disconnector lever is pushed forward. Before you load it, look through the barrel for any obstruction, and check the barrel is marked for 3-inch shells before you fire 3-inch shells: a 3-inch magnum in a 2 3/4-inch chamber causes dangerously high pressure.
